status: Research-grade change questions, not an exhaustive historically established edition
priority: After Ṣadrā's Asfār (17th c onward), with post-Tajrīd background (13th c onward). Some later Safavid works are contemporary, not necessarily chronologically later than every Asfār passage.
sourceMethod: No conjectural Arabic or Persian quotation: direct record ids link to existing working editions; original witnesses must be checked for full-context translations.

dossiers.title: What is really made? Quiddity versus particular existence
dossiers.thesis: Lāhījī's independent Gawhar treats a produced actual quiddity as the original made thing, while Narāqī's Lamaʿāt gives priority to the particular actuality of existence. The contrast cannot be dissolved into a single stock school label.
dossiers.before: Avicenna's problem of simple/compound making; Ṭūsī's Tajrīd and its glosses develop objections about contingency and relation.

sources.claim: Lāhījī calls made quiddity the view of the critical investigators.
Why making the relation itself yields regress.
How Lāhījī interprets the apricot dictum; not an independent Ibn Sīnā witness.
The producer gives a particular actuality rather than external relations among two self-existing things.
Conceptual distinction yet external unity of essence and existence.

dossiers.change: Not a universal movement from 'essence' to 'existence': later writers make different commitments about the made object, levels of abstraction and extra-mental grounding.
dossiers.unique: Gawhar pp.278–282 and Narāqī's separate Lamaʿāt passages are not textual copies of the Tajrīd sourcebook.
dossiers.tajrid: Use Tajrīd's Shawāriq p.90–91 and distinct jaʿl glosses only as comparative historical background; avoid re-collating them.
dossiers.gap: Collate complete Narāqī pp.73–81 and later Qajar authors on jaʿl; independently source the Bahmanyār–Ibn Sīnā aphorism.

dossiers.title: Unity of existential ground without collapsing all individuals
dossiers.phase: Later Safavid after Akbarian and Illuminationist debates
dossiers.thesis: Lāhījī reports several meanings of waḥdat al-wujūd, criticizes a universal-being analogy, and distinguishes one unconditioned existential ground from the multiple dependent realities.
dossiers.before: Akbarian expressions of one reality, Sufi witnessing and Avicennian causal dependence offer different possible explanations of unity.

sources.claim: The Sufi descent/manifestation claim is reported, not silently endorsed.
Self-existing reality is unlike an indeterminate natural universal needing determination.
One necessary existential ground, many actual dependent truths.
Collective unity versus identity with each single existent; source attribution remains qualified.

dossiers.change: Not straightforwardly Sadrian, Peripatetic or Akbarian: categories are reconciled or distinguished in a new independent Persian argument.
dossiers.unique: A complete seven-page Section III, not a borrowed Tajrīd lemma.
dossiers.tajrid: Tajrīd's *nafs al-amr* / ʿayn material is conceptual backdrop; do not import speculative Sufi conclusions into Ṭūsī's matn.
dossiers.gap: Separate readings from Ṣadrā's Asfār on unity and from Qūnawī/Jāmī; identify the unnamed eminent thinkers cited at p.289.

dossiers.title: The number and causal function of the intellects remain debatable
dossiers.thesis: Lāhījī maintains a tenth form-bestowing intellect while conceding the argument does not prove ten is the maximum; the Suhrawardian fixed-star objection is answered by mediated causal combinations.
dossiers.before: Classical Avicennian Rule of One and separate-intellect cosmology, with Suhrawardian objections to fixed celestial principles.

sources.claim: No proof excludes intellects beyond the standard ten.
Twelve possible derivative effects can be described from the simplified third causal level.
The tenth intellect is assigned rational souls and species forms in a historically specific cosmology.

dossiers.change: Causal hierarchy is preserved but its standard number is not treated as demonstrated maximum; form-bestowal survives without requiring a separate horizontal species-lord for every natural kind.
dossiers.unique: Gawhar Sections IV and VI; earlier Tajrīd commentary must not substitute.
dossiers.tajrid: Cite the sourcebook for earlier cosmological kalām objections; philosophical reconstruction belongs to independent Gawhar and the Ishārāt commentaries.
dossiers.gap: Verify original Ṭūsī commentary and Suhrawardī objection, plus late Ottoman and Indian revisions to cosmic-intellect theory.

dossiers.title: Natural form-bestowal survives alongside real material preparation
dossiers.phase: Later Safavid and post-Avicennian natural philosophy
dossiers.thesis: The transition from friction-only elemental generation to matter's preparation and separately received species form is explicit in consecutive Gawhar Sections V–VI.
dossiers.before: Avicenna's Shifāʾ IX.5 refutes bare matter and assigns physical preparation and separate form-bestowal differing roles.

sources.claim: Friction-only generation is rejected because the theory presupposes body without any determinate form.
Lāhījī narrates the rejected hypothesis before rejecting it.
Intrinsic matter/form and celestial/preparatory causes are distinguished.
Mixtures prepare matter for new specific forms.
Which separate intellect supplies the forms is answered next.

dossiers.change: Lāhījī is not simply a critic who abolished separate form-bestowal; the traditional causal levels remain, but their interplay is elaborated.
dossiers.unique: Consecutive Gawhar V–VI natural philosophy is an independent Persian passage, not a duplicate Tajrīd gloss.
dossiers.tajrid: Tajrīd sourcebook concerns scholastic objections to causality; do not copy its entire commentary chain into the natural philosophy reader.
dossiers.gap: Acquire contextual post-Ṣadrian Shifāʾ natural-physics glosses, Jilwa, Khwānsārī and Khayrābādī before extrapolating fate of Giver of Forms.

dossiers.title: Ontological dependence does not specify the time of the event
dossiers.thesis: A contingent being's existential cause and the additional cause specifying when a temporal event begins are distinct explanatory tasks.
dossiers.before: Avicenna's VI.1–2 differentiates enduring existential causes from successive preparatory motions.

sources.claim: Continuous motion permits changing conditions without an infinite simultaneous essential regress.
Contingency is distinct from temporal beginning.
Mubqiya and muḥditha characterize conserving versus time-specifying causes.
Material preparedness explains why this effect occurs now under classical celestial movements.

dossiers.change: A developed late teaching articulation of why-at-all versus why-now, not a new proof that Avicenna lacked vertical dependence.
dossiers.unique: Gawhar VII and Sarmāya as independent writings, not reprinted Tajrīd glosses.
dossiers.tajrid: Only link to Tajrīd for complete-cause/modal preliminaries already collated there.
dossiers.gap: Contemporary physical implementation of celestial assumptions is untenable; reconstruct which causal distinction survives independently.

dossiers.title: Approval, deliberative purpose and necessity through willing
dossiers.thesis: Lāhījī distinguishes non-acquisitive divine riḍā from goal-seeking qaṣd; later post-Tajrīd reports contest whether necessity through will is compatible with genuine alternatives.
dossiers.before: The complete-cause necessity problem, divine simplicity, free creation and sources such as Qūshjī and Khafrī are debated in Tajrīd commentary chains.

sources.claim: Could aiming at another's benefit imply acquisition of perfection in God?
Divine riḍā is contrasted with human qaṣd.
Al-Khafrī's doubt is reported through Astarābādī, not read as an independent Khafrī manuscript.
Aquinas argues for freedom to withhold conserving action.

dossiers.change: The metaphysical notion of necessity is not identical to a thesis about voluntary agency; later authors redefine the question.
dossiers.unique: Gawhar's divine-will chapter is new; Astarābādī volume II is not the same locus as Tajrīd's volume I collation.
dossiers.tajrid: The Tajrīd project remains responsible for original Qūshjī/Khafrī/Jurjānī matn–sharḥ–ḥāshiya collation. Cross-link rather than duplicate.
dossiers.gap: Verify direct original Khafrī, Qūshjī and two Khwānsārī glosses; distinguish actual freedom from conditional power.

dossiers.title: Second intentions and the ontology of attributes
dossiers.thesis: Narāqī distinguishes being qua being's general attributes from logical properties that require an intelligible object; he also reports a variant involving a negation.
dossiers.before: Rāzian logical theories, Taftāzānī/Jurjānī mental-existence arguments and Avicenna's claim that metaphysics has the most general subject.

sources.claim: General attributes of being are not automatically identical with logical second intentions.
The metaphysical science treats what is common to the special sciences.
Narāqī reports the presence or omission of lā in some copies.

dossiers.change: Late metaphysical logic develops distinctions between real-grounded abstractions and a hierarchy of conceptual predication.
dossiers.unique: Direct Narāqī Shifāʾ commentary is not among the Tajrīd sourcebook's 47 work inventory.
dossiers.tajrid: Tajrīd's Taftāzānī p.79 and related mental-existence passages are shared background, not new independent collations.
dossiers.gap: Check Avicennian original lemma and Narāqī's alternate witness; collate Abharī/Shamsiyya commentaries and later Indian logic.

dossiers.title: Substantial motion and its later critics remain undercollated
dossiers.thesis: Ṣadrā's substantial motion redefines continuity in existence; later critics must be assessed through complete objection-and-reply units, not by calling any physical change 'substantial motion'.
dossiers.before: Classical Avicennian alteration, elemental generation and hylomorphic persistence.

sources.claim: Reports Lāhījī's persistence objection; primary source of full rebuttal to be collated.
Provides selected Sadrian counterargument but not an independent full Asfār edition.

sources.locator: al-Hadiyya original 1904 pp.92–94 through modern quotation
sources.claim: Material heat transformation is a different question from continuous substantial motion.

dossiers.change: This is a **research question**, not a verified lineage of all critics. Further post-Asfār source acquisition is needed.
dossiers.unique: Jilwa/Sabzawārī/Zunūzī original texts would make this distinct; not yet translated here.
dossiers.tajrid: Tajrīd is background only; do not retranslate the old matn to substitute for Qajar objections.
dossiers.gap: Direct Arabic/Persian of Jilwa, Āqā ʿAlī Zunūzī, Sabzawārī and Khwānsārī on substantial motion; independently collate Ṣadrā's Asfār sections.

dossiers.title: Ottoman natural-philosophy commentary after the Hidāya
dossiers.thesis: The Abharī–Maybudī–Lārī commentary chain became an important vehicle of Ottoman Avicennian natural philosophy; this is not reducible to Tajrīd dogmatics.
dossiers.before: Abharī's Hidāyat al-ḥikma; Maybudī's commentary and Lārī's glosses.
dossiers.change: A possible development in the teaching of place, void, motion, matter and causal power that requires lemma-anchored primary comparison.
dossiers.unique: This natural-philosophy chain is not the same source family as the Tajrīd reader.
dossiers.tajrid: Link to Tajrīd for shared metaphysics only, not its main translated corpus.
dossiers.gap: No direct edition of the full Abharī–Maybudī–Lārī lemma/reply complex is yet acquired; source lead: Cem Türköz 2026 dissertation.

dossiers.title: South Asian teaching, natural change and the later scholastic network
dossiers.thesis: Different Indian scholarly lines carry later Avicennian, Ṣadrian and kalām arguments through Hidāya, Mīr Zāhid's glosses and Khayrābādī's natural philosophy.
dossiers.before: Shifāʾ and Hidāya commentaries, Ṣadrian commentary on Hidāya, and Arabic–Persian Dars-e-Niẓāmī transmission.

sources.claim: Mīr Zāhid is cited, not independently collated.
Five physical counterarguments do not establish his full form-bestowal doctrine.

dossiers.change: A distinct reception that cannot be explained by a linear Persian Ṣadrian succession; original source study required.
dossiers.unique: Indian lexicon and al-Hadiyya physics are not identical Tajrīd matn or its Persian gloss.
dossiers.tajrid: Only crosslink where the same Mīr Zāhid/Khwānsārī lemma is already collated, not generic Indian author matches.
dossiers.gap: Direct printed/handwritten Mīr Zāhid, Khayrābādī, Qāḍī Mubārak, original Sadrian Hidāya; Panzeca's manuscript study maps required corpora.

dossiers.title: Qajar disputes over existence, soul and motion
dossiers.thesis: Narratives of a single late Persian school obscure different philosophical responses by Narāqī, ʿAlī Nūrī, Sabzawārī, Jilwa and Zunūzī.
dossiers.before: Ṣadrā's Asfār, later Safavid Avicennism and perennial Shifāʾ–Ishārāt teaching.

sources.claim: A specific existence-first argument is available, but its whole surrounding chapter is not.

dossiers.change: Cannot yet conclude whether named later authors adopt or reject each technical Ṣadrian thesis. The independence of these debates is itself an important historiographical finding.
dossiers.unique: Original independent Qajar treatises will be the main objects; no duplication of Tajrīd chain.
dossiers.tajrid: Tajrīd provides concept genealogy, not the late Tehran question's primary corpus.
dossiers.gap: Collect Jilwa's glosses, Sabzawārī Sharḥ-i manẓūma and Zunūzī Badāyiʿ al-ḥikam with full argument context.

dossiers.title: From mental representation to knowledge as a mode of being
dossiers.thesis: The Sadrian claim that knowing is a mode of existence revises accounts of mental existence, abstraction and intentional relationship; later acceptance/resistance is not yet adequately traced.
dossiers.before: Taftāzānī–Jurjānī's mental-existence objections, the separate epistemic functions of the Active Intellect, and Avicenna's Shifāʾ.

sources.claim: Distinguishes metaphysical attributes and logical second intentions.
Denial of mental existence through heat/mountain objection.

dossiers.change: A distinct problem requiring reception history, not a retroactive claim that every thinker moved from mental form to presential cognition.
dossiers.unique: The direct later issue concerns how post-Ṣadrian commentators incorporate or reject epistemology; older Tajrīd readings are linked only.
dossiers.tajrid: Tajrīd owns the inherited Taftāzānī/Jurjānī primary collation; no need to re-extract it here.
dossiers.gap: Collate Asfār ʿilm sections, Fayḍ, Qājār responses, and the original Narāqī commentary in full.
